subject: chemistry
question_text: What is the significance of ψ and ψ²?

verification.note: PREDICTED, not asked. This question is not listed in the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section; it comes from the enumeration sweep of the Atomic Structure syllabus against the standard question archetypes. Both the question and the 1+1 mark split are claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25: the meanings of ψ and ψ² verified against NCERT Class-11 conventions; one memory tip reworded to say what squaring gives (explanation text only, marked lines and marks untouched).

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: ψ
lines: ψ is the wave function of the electron.
It is the solution of Schrödinger's wave
equation and has no direct physical meaning
It describes the amplitude of the electron wave.
steps.why: The wave function is a mathematical description of the electron wave, and its value can be positive or negative. A negative amplitude cannot be a physical quantity on its own, which is why ψ itself is not measurable.
common_mistakes: Saying ψ gives the probability. That is ψ², not ψ.
Calling ψ the path of the electron. It is a wave function, not a path.
steps.memory_tip: ψ is the wave itself and can be negative. Squaring it gives the probability density.
steps.margin_note: Naming Schrödinger's equation is worth one line here.

steps.label: ψ²

lines.text: ψ² gives the probability of finding the electron

lines: It is the probability density at a point
The region where ψ² is large is the orbital.
Where ψ² = 0, that region is a node.
steps.why: Squaring removes the sign, so ψ² is always positive and can stand for a probability. This is the step that turns the mathematics into the picture of an orbital that the rest of the chapter uses.
common_mistakes: Saying ψ² gives the position of the electron. It gives only the probability.
Leaving out the link to the orbital, which is what the question is really testing.
steps.memory_tip: Square the wave function to get probability. High ψ² means the orbital, zero ψ² means a node.
steps.margin_note: Mentioning the node connects this to the node and nodal plane question.
